claims.event: Native of Guangling who served Sun Ce, warned him against exposing himself in battle, was kept at the Xu court, dissuaded Cao Cao from attacking Wu in mourning and counselled Sun Quan at Hefei.
Erudite under whom Zhang Hong studied at the Imperial Academy.
Taught Zhang Hong the Han Odes, Record of Rites and Zuo Commentary at Waihuang.
Grand commandant who tried to hire Zhang Hong as a clerk.
Minister of works who tried to hire Zhang Hong as a clerk.
Founder of the southeastern lordship whom Zhang Hong served, refusing to release Hong to Lü Bu.
Shared strategic counsel and drafting duties with Zhang Hong; honored by Sun Quan as Lord Zhang.
Seized Xu Province and tried to summon Zhang Hong, who despised him.
Privy treasurer who befriended Zhang Hong and wrote to him while he held the rear.
Minister of works who kept Zhang Hong at court, accepted his advice not to attack Wu and posted him to Kuaiji.
Successor of Sun Ce whom Zhang Hong counselled, notably restraining his charge at Hefei.
Named in Zhang Hong’s memorial praising the Sun house for opposing him.
Guangling warden who nominated Zhang Hong and was killed by Ze Rong; Hong arranged an heir for his rites.
Attacked and killed Zhao Yu, the Guangling warden who had nominated Zhang Hong.
Langya administrator who appointed a Zhao boy to maintain Zhao Yu’s cult at Zhang Hong’s request.
Han general cited by Kong Rong in his letter to Zhang Hong as an exemplar of a frustrated commander.
Cited by Kong Rong in his letter urging Zhang Hong to return north, as a model of ending warfare.

label.en: Commandant of the Eastern Division of Kuaiji

claims.event: Urged Sun Quan to make Moling his capital, left a deathbed testament on rulership to his son Jing, and wrote verse admired by Chen Lin.
Accepted Zhang Hong’s and Liu Bei’s advice to make Moling his capital and wept on reading Hong’s testament.
Stayed at Moling on his eastern visit and urged Sun Quan to make it his capital.
Chu king said by Zhang Hong to have founded Moling, then called Jinling.
Toured past Jinling and had its ridge cut and the place renamed Moling, per the elders cited by Zhang Hong.
Commentator who objects that the Annals of Emperor Xian wrongly makes Sun Quan choose Moling on his own.
Son to whom the dying Zhang Hong handed his farewell testament.
Northern writer who showed Zhang Hong’s pillow rhapsody to others and exchanged admiring letters with him.
Named by his style Jingxing (rendered Yu Fan) in Chen Lin’s reply as one of the great writers in the south.
Named in Chen Lin’s reply alongside Zhang Hong as a great writer in the south.
Received Zhang Hong’s self-written letters in seal script and praised them in reply.
Son of Zhang Hong, scrupulous and high-minded, who rose to governor of Nan commandery and ministerial secretary.
Grandson of Zhang Hong whose quick wit offended Sun Hao; spared death by Cen Hun’s petition, then exiled to Jian’an and executed.
Promoted Zhang Shang, took offense at his zither anecdote and his comparison with Confucius, and had him arrested and later executed.
Ruler in Zhang Shang’s anecdote whom Music Master Kuang judged unworthy to hear the Qingjiao air.
Music master in Zhang Shang’s anecdote who refused to play Qingjiao for Duke Ping.
Invoked by Sun Hao, who took Zhang Shang’s goblet remark as comparing him with Confucius who never became king.
Led over a hundred officials to petition at the palace, getting Zhang Shang’s death sentence commuted.
Countryman of Zhang Hong, styled Wenbiao, who shared Sun Ce’s favor and counsel and died young.
Countryman of Zhang Hong, styled Zizheng, who shared Sun Ce’s favor and counsel and died young.
Favored and took counsel from Zhang Hong, Qin Song and Chen Duan.
Pengcheng scholar recommended by Zhang Zhao, who refused Lu Su’s command at Lukou, served as envoy to Shu, and was dismissed for warning Liu Ying.
Refugee scholar in Jiangdong renowned and friendly with Yan Jun and Bu Zhi.
Renowned with Yan Jun and Zhuge Jin; as chancellor treated Zheng Chong as family.
Introduced Yan Jun to Sun Quan.
Appointed Yan Jun, dismissed him over Liu Ying, and summoned Cheng Bing as tutor to his heir.
General whose death left the Lukou command that Yan Jun refused.
Shu chancellor who formed a high opinion of the envoy Yan Jun.
Guangling recluse scholar who feigned illness to refuse Sun Quan’s summons, was exposed attending his brother’s funeral, and was spared.
Younger brother of Liu Ying who died in office as governor of Lingling.
Son of Yan Jun who rose to privy treasurer of Shengping.
Xiapi scholar, styled Yanhuang, who debated Guan Zhong and Zilu with Yan Jun and argued ancient worthies with his son.
Exchanged essays with Yan Jun and Pei Xuan on Guan Zhong and Zilu.
Ancient minister debated in essays by Yan Jun, Pei Xuan and Zhang Cheng.
Disciple of Confucius debated in essays by Yan Jun, Pei Xuan and Zhang Cheng.
Son of Pei Xuan who debated the ranking of ancient worthies with him and whose writing the heir Deng admired.
Ancient ruler whom Pei Xuan and Pei Qin debated ranking.
Ancient ruler whom Pei Xuan and Pei Qin debated ranking.
Ancient worthy whom Pei Xuan and Pei Qin debated ranking.
Runan scholar of the Five Classics, chief clerk to Shi Xie, then tutor to Sun Quan’s heir Deng, whom he lectured on marriage.
Classicist under whom Cheng Bing studied.
Scholar in Jiaozhou with whom Cheng Bing debated the classics.
Appointed Cheng Bing his chief clerk.
Father of the bride whom Cheng Bing escorted from Wu for the heir Deng.
Daughter of Zhou Yu betrothed to the heir Deng and escorted from Wu by Cheng Bing.
Henan scholar of the Changes and Zuo, styled Zihe, born a Li, recommended by Yan Jun to instruct the heir.

label.en: Prefect of the Masters of Writing

claims.event: Kuaiji scholar who copied books to study, distilled ritual texts for the two palaces, counselled against cruel punishment of Lü Yi and predicted Cao Pi’s early death.
Employed and consulted Kan Ze, read Jia Yi at his suggestion, and grieved his death.
Author of the essay On the Faults of Qin, which Kan Ze recommended to Sun Quan.
Official whose treachery was exposed; Kan Ze dissuaded burning and dismemberment as his punishment.
Praised Kan Ze as Wu’s Yang Xiong and today’s Dong Zhongshu, per the Wu lu.
Han writer to whom Kan Ze was compared.
Han Confucian to whom Kan Ze was compared.
Wei Emperor Wen whose early death Kan Ze predicted from the graph of his name.
Notes Sun Quan was only five years older than Cao Pi, and discusses variant readings of the Shu riddle.
Danyang Confucian, styled Zizheng, who annotated the Guoyu, Gongyang and Guliang and was honored by Lu Xun and others.
Bowed to Tang Gu as a teacher.
Bowed to Tang Gu as a teacher.
Bowed to Tang Gu as a teacher.
Scholar from Pei who served under Shi Xie and Sun Quan in the far south, sailed with Lü Dai and silenced the Shu envoy Zhang Feng with a riddle.
Qi lord enfeoffed at Xue, ancestor of Xue Zong’s clan.
Grandson of Lord Mengchang who refused restoration and settled in Zhuyi, founding the Xue clan line.
Teacher of Xue Zong in Jiaozhou.
Submitted to Sun Quan and appointed Xue Zong.
Inspector who led the southern expedition to Jiuzhen; Xue Zong memorialized on his successor when he was recalled.
Shu envoy who mocked Kan Ze’s name and was silenced by Xue Zong’s riddle on Shu.
Shu envoy who traded character riddles on Shu and Wu with Zhuge Ke at the Wu court.
Answered Fei Yi’s riddles on the graphs for Shu and Wu.

label.en: Supervisor of the Masters of Writing
General of the Household Gentlemen of the Five Offices

claims.event: Ancient sage king who, per Xue Zong’s memorial, toured the south and died at Cangwu.
Built his power at Panyu and subdued the Yue chieftains, per Xue Zong’s memorial.
Destroyed Lü Jia, created nine southern commanderies and an inspector of Jiaozhi.
Southern leader destroyed by Emperor Wu of Han.
Governor in Jiaozhi who taught plowing and civilized customs.
Governor of Jiuzhen who taught plowing, marriage ritual and schooling.
Nanhai man posted to Rinan who beat his chief clerk to death over a meagre welcome and was driven out.
Jiuzhen governor who caned Fan Xin to death at a banquet for his father-in-law and was killed by Fan Miao’s poisoned arrows.
Father-in-law of Dan Meng who refused to dance with Fan Xin at the banquet.
Merit clerk who pressed Zhou Jing to dance and was caned to death by Dan Meng.
Younger brother of Fan Xin who stormed the commandery office and killed Dan Meng with poisoned arrows.
Jiaozhi governor who failed to subdue Fan Miao’s band.
Kuaiji man, former inspector, who staffed districts with cronies, provoked revolt, fled to sea and died.
Hometown crony whom Zhu Fu made a local official, oppressing the people.
Hometown crony whom Zhu Fu made a local official, oppressing the people.
Nanyang man who feuded with Liu Biao, exhausted his generals and was killed.
Feuded with Zhang Jin and sent Wu Ju to govern Cangwu.
Kindly Lingling elder ignorant of affairs, driven out after clashing with Wu Ju.
Changsha soldier sent by Liu Biao to govern Cangwu who refused to defer to Lai Gong and drove him out.
Sent to the south, rooted out Zhang Jin’s old officers and restored order before recall.
Old officer of Zhang Jin rooted out by Bu Zhi.
Old officer of Zhang Jin rooted out by Bu Zhi.
Arrived during the Shi family rebellion; Xue Zong urged a careful successor if he did not return south.
Marquis of Jianchang camped at Banzhou who took Xue Zong as chief clerk and tutor.
Chief clerk to Sun Lü, then secretariat official who memorialized against Sun Quan’s personal campaign on Liaodong.
Submitted then rebelled, enraging Sun Quan into planning a personal campaign.
Planned to campaign against Gongsun Yuan in person but desisted after Xue Zong’s memorial.
Cited by Xue Zong for his remark about sailing away on a raft.
Cited by Xue Zong as delighted by Confucius’s raft remark.
Cited by Xue Zong as wishing to ride the war barges until Xue Guangde objected.
Cited by Xue Zong for threatening to cut his throat to stop Emperor Yuan boarding the war barges.
Ancient strongman cited by Xue Zong as powerless at sea.

label.en: Supervisor of the Masters of Writing

claims.event: Had Xue Zong improvise ancestral prayers and gave him a purple ribbon bag as tutor to the heir.
Improvised ancestral prayers for Sun Quan, headed appointments and tutored the heir; his works and line were honored by his sons.
Son of Xue Zong who reported on Shu’s decay to Sun Xiu after a horse-buying mission and died returning from Jiaozhi.
Sent Xue Xu to Shu for horses and promoted Xue Ying on his accession.
Son of Xue Zong, styled Daoyan, who continued his father’s work, compiled the Book of Wu, was exiled over the Sheng Creek canal, drafted Sun Hao’s surrender and served Jin.
Promoted, jailed, exiled and recalled Xue Ying, and surrendered to Jin with letters Ying drafted.
Proposed cutting the Sheng Creek channel; his later execution led to Xue Ying’s jailing.
Memorialized that Xue Ying be recalled to finish the Book of Wu.
Han historian praised by Hua He as a genius of his age.
Han historian praised by Hua He as a genius of his age.
Set to drafting the Book of Wu, judged by Hua He to lack a historian’s gift.
Set with Ding Fu to drafting the Book of Wu, judged inadequate by Hua He.
The Lesser Emperor who appointed five scholars including Xue Ying to compile the Book of Wu.
One of the five compilers of the Book of Wu, later fell to treason charges.
One of the five compilers of the Book of Wu, who died early.
One of the five compilers of the Book of Wu, who died early.
Principled appointments official demoted to Hengyang and jailed after visiting Xue Ying.
Jin commander to whom Sun Hao sent a surrender letter drafted by Xue Ying.
Jin commander to whom Sun Hao sent a surrender letter drafted by Xue Ying.
Jin commander to whom Sun Hao sent a surrender letter drafted by Xue Ying.
Author of the Jin ji recording Xue Ying’s answer on why Sun Hao fell.
Asked Xue Ying why Sun Hao perished and about Wu scholars.
Son of Xue Ying, styled Lingzhang, who became governor of Danyang and junior tutor under Emperor Yuan.
Under whose reign Xue Jian rose to Danyang and junior tutor.
Praised in the historian’s verdict as principled and ranked by Sun Ce just below Zhang Zhao.
Ranked Zhang Hong just below Zhang Zhao, per the verdict.
Ranked by Sun Ce just above Zhang Hong, per the verdict.
Praised in the verdict as a scholar who refused office to save an old friend.
Praised in the verdict among the leading scholars of the time.
Praised in the verdict among the leading scholars of the time.
